Hi Ben,

Thanks for taking this. We have a short security questionnaire as part of Aurora's procurement. A few items where we need specific language/commitments from Redwood for your hosted API:

1) Where are customer request payloads, generated outputs, and model caches persisted geographically? Any cross-region replication?
2) What is the maximum time user data (request + response) may exist in persistent storage vs ephemeral caches?
3) Snapshot / backup retention window for hosted model state and infrastructure snapshots (and whether these can be scoped to region).
4) Are backups encrypted at rest with customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) options?
5) How do you validate deletion requests (customer-initiated tenant wipe) and provide evidence?

If you can send a short, plain-language response for each and any relevant artifacts (one-pager, matrix, or attestations), that would be great. Aim for language we can include in our security review doc.

Hi Liam — thanks for the clear list. Answers below at a high level; attaching a short summary PDF and a matrix (retention_matrix.xlsx) for your legal/ops docset. If you need formal wording for a contract/annex, let me know and I can loop in Legal.

1) Geography / persistence- Request payloads and generated output are stored in the same cloud region selected for your tenant (we have region selector at onboarding). We do not proactively replicate customer request/response data cross-region. Persisted artifacts: request + response logs (for debugging/metrics), per-tenant KV cache snapshots when enabled, and encrypted object store snapshots used for disaster recovery. Model artifacts are read-only and shared across tenants; only tenant-derived artifacts are region-scoped.

2) Retention windows (persistent vs ephemeral)- Ephemeral: in-memory KV cache and serving-layer caches are transient and typically expire within minutes to hours (configurable TTL; default 1 hour). Persistent logs: request/response logs are retained by default for 30 days in hosted mode (configurable down to 0 days for strict customers). If you enable longer retention for debugging, that is opt-in and documented in the tenant config.

3) Snapshots / backups- Infrastructure-level snapshots (VM/GPU images) and object-store backups are retained for 90 days by default for recovery purposes; we can support shorter retention windows per contract for regulatory customers. Backups are region-scoped; we do not copy recovery snapshots to other regions unless customer has explicitly enabled cross-region replication for disaster recovery.

4) Encryption & KMS- All persisted customer data is encrypted at rest using AES-256. We support provider-managed KMS by default and can integrate with customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own key) for Private deployments; for hosted, CMK support can be enabled under enterprise contracts.

5) Deletion and proof- For customer-initiated tenant wipes we: (a) mark data for deletion, (b) remove tenant objects from active stores and caches, (c) purge backups/snapshots within defined retention cutover windows, and (d) provide an attestation record including timestamps and an operations ticket. We can provide a deletion evidence pack (audit log excerpts + object keys) within 5 business days.

Attachments: redwood_hosted-data-retention-summary.pdf, retention_matrix.xlsx

If you want, I can produce a succinct clause you can paste into your procurement doc. Is Aurora's procurement deal id DA-4421?

Subject: Re: Data residency + snapshot retention questions (hosted API) — evidence pack and clarifications

Hi Liam — attaching the summary and a retention matrix for Aurora (see files). A few clarifications based on your anticipated review items:

• Default retention windows are conservative and configurable. If you require shorter guarantees, we will include specific retention SLA language in the order form.

• Snapshots/backups: operationally, object-store snapshots targeted for a tenant are placed in the same cloud region and queued for purge when a wipe is requested. The purge work is typically completed within 72 business hours; our compliance team will compile the evidence (audit log extract) within 5 business days.

• Cross-region replication: not performed by default for tenant data. Disaster recovery replication is an opt-in that is documented and requires explicit authorization.

• KMS/CMK: for hosted customers we offer managed keys by default; CMK configuration via partner KMS can be provided under enterprise agreements (we can outline the integration steps for your security team).

Next steps: I can (A) provide a short contract clause wording for Aurora's procurement, (B) hand off the formal evidence pack once Ops/Compliance produce it, or (C) schedule a 30-min call to walk through specifics. Which would you prefer?

Best,
Ben
